subject: Human Evolution
title: Göbekli Tepe
description: A micro-lesson that makes Göbekli Tepe usable.

hook.text: In Turkey, massive carved stone pillars stand in circles—built 11,600 years ago by hunter-gatherers, not farmers.

buildup.text: Göbekli Tepe's pillars weigh up to 10 tons, carved with foxes, vultures, snakes, and abstract symbols.

discovery.text: Building it required hundreds of workers, suggesting complex social organization before agriculture.

twist.text: Some archaeologists now think ritual sites like this drove farming—you needed to feed the builders.

climax.text: Göbekli Tepe overturns the idea that farming came first and civilization followed. It may be the reverse.

punchline.text: Belief may have invented farming, not the reverse.

quiz.question: Why is Göbekli Tepe significant?
options: It shows complex social organization before agriculture
It was built by early farmers
